input: Audience: Wedding-venue owners whose couples book tours more than two weeks ahead and who cannot readily add weekend or early-morning appointments. | Tension: Couples may choose another venue before a delayed tour, but the venue has genuine limits on staffing, event preparation, and when a space is ready to show. | Argument: When couples book a venue tour well in advance, the business may need to keep the venue in consideration without expanding into tour times that do not fit its staffing or preparation constraints. A personalized preview before the visit is a possible alternative to treating schedule expansion as the only response. | Take: For couples who must wait, consider whether a personal call, virtual preview, or useful supplemental message could answer questions and help them picture the venue before their in-person tour. | Mechanism: The venue owner said couples sometimes found another venue before their scheduled visit, while also describing limits on Saturday tours and drawbacks to Sunday appointments. Whitney proposed a phone or video touchpoint and a supplemental message for people whose tours were booked farther out; these were ideas, not tested interventions. | Reader decision: For tours booked well in advance, decide whether to preserve the current schedule and add a feasible pre-tour touchpoint, or whether a different appointment option is workable for the business.
